title: `detail-section` still offers `headerColor` as a free-form `string` input, so the SDUI authoring surface invites values the published validator now refuses
body:
Filed unassigned by the seat implementing #6594 (session `session_01PBjwYLS6BciTQW3c9xQiD2`). Out of that card's scope, which is the `@object-ui/types` mirror only. Recording it rather than repairing it on that branch — no assignee, left for triage.

## What was observed

`packages/plugin-detail/src/index.tsx:336`, in the `detail-section` registration:

```ts
{ name: 'headerColor', type: 'string', label: 'Header Color' },
```

That declaration is unchanged since before the vocabulary was ruled. As of #6594 the key's contract is a **closed six-token enum** — `muted`, `muted/50`, `accent`, `primary/10`, `secondary/10`, `destructive/10` — on both `DetailViewSection.headerColor` and the `@object-ui/types/zod` mirror, matching `@objectstack/spec`'s strict `record:details` section schema (maintainer ruling A, 2026-08-26, objectstack#12126).

So the two ends now disagree about what an author may write: the registration says "any string", the validator says "one of six".

## Why it is worth a card

`inputs` is not documentation — `recordDetailsInputs.spec-parity.test.ts` in the same package spells out why: `gen-manifest.ts` serializes it into `sdui.manifest.json` (the save-gate and parser whitelist) and into `sdui-intrinsics.d.ts` (the JSX authoring surface). An author working through that surface is offered a free-text field for a key whose only valid values are six tokens, gets no completion and no rejection at authoring time, and finds out at parse time — or, for the values that used to render by accident, not at all.

This is the value-level twin of the key-level class `scripts/check-designer-field-key-parity.mjs` was built for (objectui#5761 / #6223): a designer offering something the spec refuses. That gate compares KEY SETS and covers the metadata designers, so neither half of it sees this instance.

## Reproduction

1. `git grep -n "headerColor" packages/plugin-detail/src/index.tsx` — one hit, `type: 'string'`.
2. Compare against `packages/types/src/zod/views.zod.ts`, where `DetailViewSectionSchema.headerColor` is a `z.enum` of the six.
3. Any value outside the six is refused at parse with `headerColor` named in the error path, while the manifest still accepts it as a valid `string`.

## Notes for whoever picks this up

- Check first whether `ComponentInput` can carry an option list at all, and whether the designer renders one — `packages/types/src/base.ts` is the declaration, and it was in flight on another card at the time of filing, so read it fresh rather than trusting this line.
- The renderer's verbatim `bg-*` pass-through is deliberately **undeclared** (ruling A rejected declaring it, since whether the class renders depends on the host app's Tailwind build). Whatever the input offers, it must not turn that affordance into a promise.
- Related, no dependency in either direction: #6594 narrowed the contract; #6178 is where the six tokens came from.
